findings.text: Board.tsx renders data-column={status} in both the mobile panel (line 264) and the desktop grid (line 305), so every e2e [data-column="..."] selector matches two elements. Specs work around this with .first() across ~13 files; the workaround relies on (a) mobile-first DOM ordering and (b) Playwright toContainText reading hidden DOM. Triage 2026-04-30 treated each match-failure as a separate test bug rather than fixing the structural duplication. Consider scoping the column marker to a viewport-stable attribute or hoisting the assertion onto a single Board-level element.

findings.text: E2E error-state assertions rely on a non-standard selector — no canonical data-testid for error display components defined
findings.motivation: AC-3 ('no error is shown') requires an E2E assertion on error state, but there is no stable data-testid on the app's error display components. The test initially used a non-existent data-testid selector, which could make future error-state assertions brittle or invisible (a missing element reads as no error, masking real failures).
findings.behavior: Error display components in the app do not carry a data-testid attribute; E2E tests that assert on 'no error shown' cannot reliably distinguish a hidden error state from a missing DOM node.
findings.approach: Add data-testid='error-banner' (or equivalent) to the app's top-level error display components so E2E assertions on error state are unambiguous. Document the canonical selector in the E2E README.

findings.text: Pre-commit codex review of the 3-party property spec surfaced two test-quality items in assertS5_3P (member<=>leafCount biconditional). (P2, :1218) It reads membership solely from A's page and returns early on membersA===null, so any settled state where A has left but B/C still share the group skips the S5 biconditional entirely (under-asserts; can only skip, never false-RED). This mirrors assertC0_3P's all-three-members guard (line 1109), so it is consistent with the epic's settled-full-group philosophy, but it does dilute S5 coverage on A-absent chains. (P3, :1226) The dormant degraded-form branch calls getPubkeyLeafCountHook before the !leafOk guard and then uses leafCount inside the branch it claims runs without the hook — internally inconsistent and unreachable while STRICT_FORM_AVAILABLE holds.
findings.motivation: Surfaced by the base:feature review gate (codex, read-only). No P1 issues; recorded as test-coverage-quality follow-ups for whatever story next owns the 3-party assertion bodies rather than re-opening a just-verified file in the wrap-up.
findings.behavior: No product-behavior impact (test-only). The biconditional check is skipped, not falsified, on A-absent states, and the degraded branch is dead while strict hooks are present.
findings.approach: P2: source membership from whichever actor pages still have the group loaded (or each actor's own page) so S5 still validates B/C when A has left. P3: move the getPubkeyLeafCountHook call after the !leafOk guard and make the degraded branch genuinely hook-free (positive direction via member-set only), or delete the dead branch once the l3-completion hook story lands.

findings.text: No jsdom/RTL component test layer — vitest is node-only (vitest.config.ts:6) so React component rendering and UI behavior is never unit-tested; UI fixes can only cover extracted pure helpers
findings.motivation: UI regressions (silent error degradation, disabled-button propagation, async setState races) are caught only by e2e or not at all; the node-only constraint forces every testable bit of logic out of components into .ts sidecars, and anything that genuinely needs a rendered component stays untested.
findings.behavior: vitest runs in the node environment with no jsdom and no React Testing Library. .tsx and NEXT_PUBLIC-bearing modules cannot be imported in unit tests. The DevicesTab relay-fetch fix (commit 8814292) could only unit-test a pure extracted function; the rendered component path was verified manually.
findings.approach: Decide between (a) adding a jsdom + React Testing Library project to vitest for component-level tests, or (b) a Playwright component-testing layer. Either lets UI behavior be asserted directly instead of only via pure-helper extraction.
findings.success_signal: A representative component (e.g. DevicesTab) has a rendering/interaction test that fails when its UI degradation path regresses.

findings.text: marmot-ts fork public types don't reflect runtime: identifier/d-tag mismatch is guarded locally (device-sync.ts extractSlot) but absent from the fork's .d.ts — a future fork update could silently break device loading with no tsc error
findings.motivation: We control the marmot-ts fork (CLAUDE.md), so type/runtime drift is fixable at the source instead of being papered over with consumer-side casts. Today the mismatch is caught only by a hand-written extractSlot guard + a local comment; nothing makes the contract type-checked, so a fork bump that changes d-tag extraction breaks device loading silently.
findings.behavior: marmot-ts KeyPackageManager.list returns objects whose slot field is runtime 'identifier' while the public type calls it 'd' (or vice-versa); device-sync.ts:343-353 defensively reads it. Separately, marmot-client adoptClientState emits 'updated' before 'joined', an ordering the .d.ts (which only references 'joined') does not expose — confirmed only by tracing compiled dist.
findings.approach: Fix the fork's type declarations to match runtime (identifier/d), and document the adoptClientState emit ordering in the fork types or a consumer comment. Add a type-level regression so a future fork bump that changes the shape fails tsc rather than runtime device loading.
findings.success_signal: A marmot-ts version bump that changes d-tag extraction or event ordering produces a tsc error in notestr-web, not a silent device-loading failure.

findings.text: event-side updatedByDevice ?? '' normalization has no AC in any epic
findings.motivation: The LWW guard normalizes absent device IDs on both sides of (event.updatedByDevice ?? '') < (existing.updatedByDevice ?? ''). The existing-side ?? '' is covered by existing tests ('loses to a legacy existing task whose updatedByDevice is absent'). The event-side ?? '' had no test, discovered by Stryker mutation testing — a StringLiteral mutation replacing '' with 'Stryker was here!' survived because all test device IDs use lowercase a-z (ASCII >= 100), which sort after 'S' (83), making the mutation undetectable. The invariant to spec: when an event omits updatedByDevice, it normalizes to '' (lexicographic minimum), so it wins over any existing task with a non-empty device ID under a timestamp+pubkey tie. This matters for CRDT convergence when legacy events (no device field) arrive after sibling-device events.
findings.behavior: An event with undefined updatedByDevice normalizes to '' on the left side of the device-level tie-break comparison, winning over any existing task whose updatedByDevice is a non-empty string. Pinned by four new example-based tests using device IDs 'A', 'B', 'Q', '9' (all ASCII <= 82, below 'S').

findings.text: joinFromWelcomeInvite failure classification (no_matching_kp / ciphersuite_mismatch / unknown) has no AC in any epic
findings.motivation: When an MLS welcome invite fails, the function classifies the error into one of three reasons (no_matching_kp, ciphersuite_mismatch, unknown) and records it for user-facing diagnostic display. This behaviour affects what the user sees in the failed-welcome log. No acceptance criterion in any epic specifies the classification rules or their user-visible outcome.
findings.behavior: joinFromWelcomeInvite classifies errors by regex match against err.message: /[Nn]o matching/ → no_matching_kp; /ciphersuite/ → ciphersuite_mismatch; anything else → unknown. The failureReason is persisted via appendFailedWelcome and surfaces in the UI as invite diagnostics.

archive.text: epic-e2e-relay-state-isolation: per-spec docker compose restart relay auto-fixture to wipe stale kind-30443 KeyPackages between spec files.
archive.reason: Relitigates the 2026-05-01 reversal in commit 7b31ba1. The per-spec _relayReset fixture was tried, broke 'npx playwright test' for callers without the relay container up, and masked test-design bugs behind sweeping cleanups. The standing principle (feedback_e2e_relay_independence.md) is that e2e tests must pass against any relay state via within-test isolation: pinClientSlot, rotated bunker keys, Date.now() group names, clearAppState — not fixture-level resets. If a test seems to need a clean relay, the test has a bug.

archive.text: Including kinds 443, 444, 445, 0, 1059 in NIP-46 perms list because marmot-ts documentation implied they were user-signer kinds
archive.reason: S5 implementation verified via marmot-ts dist/client/group/marmot-group.js and applesauce-common/dist/operations/gift-wrap.js: kind 443 is legacy and query-only; kind 444 is an unsigned NIP-59 rumor by design; kind 445 uses an ephemeral key via finalizeEvent; kind 1059 (gift wrap outer) also uses an ephemeral key; kind 0 is not exercised. The actual user-signer kind for sending MLS welcomes is kind 13 (NIP-59 Seal), which was absent from the original spec list. The spec's architecture context was based on marmot-ts kind numbers, not on which signing path the user signer was actually routed through.
